entities.summary:
Cresilas (b. 479 BCE, Kydonia, Crete; d. 409 BCE), a leading sculptor of the High Classical period in ancient Greece, distinguished himself through a powerful blend of idealized form and individual expression. Active primarily in Athens during its golden age under Pericles, Cresilas contributed significantly to the sculptural canon, standing alongside contemporaries like Phidias and Polycleitus. His known works, though mostly surviving through Roman copies, reveal a master craftsman adept at capturing both heroic grandeur and nuanced human emotion, influencing the trajectory of portraiture and monumental sculpture.

Among Cresilas's most celebrated achievements was his portrait bust of Pericles, which depicted the Athenian statesman with a helmet, a common motif in portraits of military leaders, yet imbued with a sense of intellectual gravitas. This work, along with his bronze statue of a Wounded Amazon, created for the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus in competition with Phidias and Polycleitus around 430 BCE, showcased his ability to render dynamic physical states and psychological depth. Other notable commissions included a statue of Diomedes and possibly a depiction of the hero Achilles, highlighting his engagement with epic themes and athletic ideals prevalent in Greek art.

Cresilas's legacy lies in his contribution to refining the High Classical style, particularly his pioneering approach to portraiture that sought to convey character alongside physical likeness. His work on Pericles, in particular, established a prototype for depicting leaders with a blend of civic virtue and personal authority, a model that resonated through Hellenistic and Roman art. The expressive force and anatomical precision of his Wounded Amazon further cemented his reputation, demonstrating how pathos could be integrated within the classical ideal of beauty, thereby broadening the emotional range of Greek sculpture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cresilas was a major sculptor of the High Classical period whose innovative portraiture and expressive monumental works significantly influenced the emotional range and character depiction in Greek and later Roman art. His contributions helped define the aesthetic ideals of his era, with his works being widely copied and admired for centuries.
